newsitem.title: POLAND: Gas net and debt on Polish premier's Sweden agenda.
newsitem.headline: Gas net and debt on Polish premier's Sweden agenda.

text.p: Polish Prime Minister Wlodzimierz Cimoszewicz said an idea for a pipeline network around the Baltic carrying North Sea gas to Poland would be among the topics of his two-day visit to Sweden starting on Tuesday.

"We will also discuss the idea we spoke of with the Danish premier, namely creating an energy, gas ring around the Baltic sea allowing us to import gas from North Sea gas fields," Cimoszewicz told public radio before leaving Warsaw.

In Warsaw in March Denmark's Prime Minister Poul Nyrup Rasmussen proposed that the two countries launch a joint study for a 20-to 30-year project to create an energy network linking Baltic region states, possibly including Russia.

Last year Poland clinched a 25-year agreement with Russia's giant state-owned Gazprom for the supply of 250 billion cubic metres of natural gas, but it has expressed interest in long-term supplies from Norway to diversify its sources of gas.
Cimoszewicz is to hold meetings with Sweden's king Carl Gustav and the speaker of parliament on Tuesday, then attend a banquet with Prime Minister Goran Persson.
On Wednesday he will hold talks with Persson, give a news conference and meet members of Sweden's Polish community.

"We want to talk about whether there is a chance at last for an agreement on Ecoconversion, that is allocating part of our debt owed to Sweden for spending in Poland on matters related to protecting the environment," Cimoszewicz said.

Other topics would include Baltic regional cooperation such as projects already launched jointly to combat cross-border crime, as well as the future expansion of the European Union which Poland hopes to join by around 2002.
